sentences.text: This saint looks peacefully asleep, but his white robes are hiding a death.
This is Saint Serapion, painted by Francisco Zurbarán in 1628.
Most people see a tired monk resting in calm white cloth.
Even the critic Tom Lubbock called the scene understated and calm.
And the picture seems to agree.
His eyes are closed and his head rests softly on his shoulder.
Ropes tie both hands to a pole.
According to the painter Alison Watt, you are seduced by this simplicity, only to realise you have been duped.
Serapion was a Mercedarian friar who fought in the Crusades and was later martyred.
Zurbarán painted him for the funeral chapel of his order in Seville.
He's a martyr, bound by both hands.
So now, do you see a sleeping monk, or a martyr?

meta.title: This saint is not asleep
meta.description: Saint Serapion was painted by Francisco Zurbarán in 1628 for the funeral chapel of the Mercedarian monastery in Seville. The calm figure in white is a martyr, tied by both wrists to a pole.
meta.question: A sleeping monk, or a martyr?
